clue.text: Conventional policeman fair about wayward boy

indicators.note: the policeman-plus-fair pair is placed around the other piece, so it sits about it

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman
OK means fair, passable

indicators.note: wayward suggests going astray, so the letters of boy wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A by-the-book officer is fair-minded towards a delinquent lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conventional' is the definition: copybook as an adjective. 'wayward' rearranges the boy, and 'about' has the policeman-and-fair pair surround that result, split after the policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Copybook as an adjective means exemplary or textbook, following the model exactly, hence conventional.

clue.text: Strike's about to restrict supply

indicators.note: about means around, so the strike word goes around the word to

parts.note: to cuff is to strike with the hand

explanation.surface: A walkout is about to limit provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action but means a blow with the hand; the possessive 's is part of that leaf, and 'about' makes it wrap the word to.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut off a supply is to stop or restrict its flow, as with gas or electricity.

clue.text: Thespian with a past

parts.note: a means per, as in so much a head
former means past or previous

explanation.surface: An actor who has a history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' means 'each', as in two pounds a head, which is PER.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is an actor, one who plays roles on stage.

clue.text: Unpleasant character, such as Shylock, when pricked

explanation.surface: A nasty figure, like Shakespeare's moneylender when stabbed.
explanation.walkthrough: Shylock in The Merchant of Venice asks 'If you prick us, do we not bleed?'; a bleeder is also British slang for a nasty person.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleeder is British slang for an unpleasant person, and literally one who bleeds when cut.

clue.text: Old choral work being performed in music-hall

parts.note: in ancient Greek drama an ode was a choral song
a show that is on is being performed

explanation.surface: An ancient sung piece is staged in a variety theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The ancient Greek building for musical performances was called an odeon, and the name became a British cinema chain.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece and Rome an odeon was a roofed building for musical performances, a hall for music.

clue.text: They dig out material for a suit

explanation.surface: Workers excavate cloth to be made into clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The suit is a suit of playing cards, not clothes, and the diggers are garden tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades are digging tools, and in cards spades are one of the four suits.

clue.text: Saw demonstrator overcoming bishop

indicators.note: in a down clue overcoming means sitting on top of, so this piece comes above

parts.note: a prover is one who proves or demonstrates something
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A demonstrator at a protest triumphs over a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is a noun, an old saying, not the past of 'see'. 'overcoming' puts PROVER over B in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional saying or maxim, the same as an adage.

clue.text: Put up indecent tapestries, initially, in abode

indicators.note: in a down entry put up means written upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: lewd means indecent or obscene

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of tapestries

explanation.surface: Someone hung rude wall hangings at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' is the reversal sign, turning LEWD into DWEL, not a hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelt means lived or resided, i.e. was in one's home.

clue.text: Permanent position

explanation.surface: A fixed post.
explanation.definitionFit: A standing army or order is permanent, and one's standing is one's status or rank.

clue.text: Novelist comes upon desert flower

indicators.note: in a down entry comes upon means placed on top of the next piece

parts.note: C. P. Snow was an English novelist
to drop is to abandon or desert

explanation.surface: A writer happens upon a bloom in the wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' is a verb, to abandon, not sandy wastes.
explanation.definitionFit: The snowdrop is a small white flower blooming in late winter.

clue.text: Cheap work from vile-sounding composer?

parts.note: the cheap work is a stage piece named after a small old coin, and the composer is Kurt Weill, whose surname sounds like vile

explanation.surface: A bargain-basement piece by a composer with an unpleasant-sounding name.
explanation.walkthrough: Kurt Weill's surname is said like 'vile'; his Brecht collaboration is named for an old British coin worth three pence, so 'cheap'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Weill–Brecht stage work's title literally names a low-value coin, so it is a cheap work by that composer.

clue.text: Defeat for Scotland following old-fashioned retreat

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made over, so the letters of old are remade in a new order

parts.note: a den is a private retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: A Scottish loss comes after an outdated hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' is split, 'fashioned' acting as the anagram sign on 'old'. Flodden (1513) was a disastrous Scottish defeat by the English.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Flodden in 1513 was a catastrophic military loss for the Scots, killing their king James IV.

clue.text: Forcibly removed or knocked off, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to knock off is to stop work, so knocked off means rested

explanation.surface: Something was taken away by force, or else simply stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: The W is silent, so 'rested' and the answer are said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest is to pull or twist away by force, so wrested means seized from someone forcibly.

clue.text: Wrong representative or political leader I backed

indicators.note: backed tells us the whole string of pieces is read from end to start

parts.note: PM, the Prime Minister, is a political leader

explanation.surface: A mistaken envoy, or a party head whom I supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses the whole of REP+OR+PM+I, giving I, MP, RO, PER.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper means incorrect or unsuitable, just as something wrong is.

clue.text: Bear repeated ridicule

indicators.note: repeated means the bear's name is given twice

parts.note: Winnie the Pooh is A. A. Milne's famous bear

explanation.surface: A bear mocked over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: The bear is A. A. Milne's Winnie the Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss something scornfully or deride it is the verb sense here.

clue.text: Animals so treated like rubbish

indicators.note: something treated like rubbish is put in the bin, so the word so goes inside

parts.note: a bin holds rubbish, and a bin is where rubbish goes

explanation.surface: Creatures thus handled as if they were waste.
explanation.walkthrough: Treating something like rubbish means binning it, so 'treated like' is the container signal. Bison is its own plural, matching 'Animals'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bison is both singular and plural, here the plural: large wild cattle of North America and Europe.

clue.text: So to covet is wrong, it's whispered

indicators.note: is wrong says the letters are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A soft reminder that envying others is a sin.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the commandment against coveting; 'is wrong' rearranges SO TO COVET.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for under the voice, the phrase describes something said in an undertone or murmur.

clue.text: One of this bunch was a reflective youth

definitions.text: One of this bunch was a reflective youth

parts.words: One of this bunch was a reflective youth
parts.note: the youth of Greek myth fell in love with his reflection and became a spring flower, which grows in bunches

explanation.surface: A group of flowers, one of whom was a vain young man gazing at himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The mythical youth who pined over his reflection gave his name to the flower; the plural is the bunch.
explanation.definitionFit: The flowers are named after the youth of myth who loved his own reflection in a pool.

clue.text: You are, I see, reportedly after article of precious metal

indicators.note: after places the heard letters behind the article

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: the phrase is taken as spoken words whose sounds are single letter names

explanation.surface: Someone observes you have come after an item made of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'You are, I see' gives the letter sounds U R I C.
explanation.definitionFit: Auric means relating to or containing gold, the precious metal (Latin aurum).

clue.text: Record set in once-ruined city

indicators.note: set in places the record inside the rearranged letters
ruined means wrecked, so the letters of once are broken up and reordered

parts.note: a log is a record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: A record is put down in a city once destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once-ruined' looks like one adjective but splits: 'ruined' turns ONCE into CONE, and 'set in' puts the record inside it. The German city was heavily bombed in the war.
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne (Köln) is a city in Germany on the Rhine.

clue.text: Corresponding by using mail service in workplace

indicators.note: in places the mail service inside the split workplace

parts.note: the word is split as work, OP for opus, plus place, a site
PO stands for Post Office, a mail service

explanation.surface: Matching up by using the post at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workplace' must be split into work, as in opus, and place; the mail service goes between the two halves, signalled by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite can mean counterpart or matching, as with an opposite number holding the corresponding post.

clue.text: Poet or philosopher, say

indicators.note: say means the philosopher's name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Herbert Spencer was a Victorian philosopher

explanation.surface: A poet, or perhaps a philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: Herbert Spencer the philosopher and the Elizabethan poet of The Faerie Queene have names said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was an Elizabethan writer of verse, author of The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: First fish caught by male (or female)

indicators.note: caught by puts the fish inside the male

parts.note: a man is a male
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: The first fish landed by a man, or a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: '(or female)' is a second, bracketed definition: a maiden is a young woman as well as first, as in a maiden voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiden as an adjective means first, as in a maiden speech or maiden voyage.

clue.text: Browbeat fielder for bloomer

parts.note: to cow is to intimidate or browbeat
slip is a cricket fielding position close behind the batsman, so a fielder there

explanation.surface: A bully intimidates a cricketer over a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a flower here, not a mistake. Slip is a cricket fielding position beside the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is something that blooms, and this yellow wild plant is a spring flower.

clue.text: This side isn't generally seen as unfair

explanation.surface: One face of the cloth is hidden, and that seems unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: The wrong side of fabric is the reverse, normally hidden from view.
explanation.definitionFit: The reverse side of cloth is the side kept out of sight, and an unjust thing is not right.

clue.text: City in Italy Rome can represent

indicators.note: represent is read as re-present, the letters presented again in another order

explanation.surface: The Italian capital stands for one of the country's cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represent' reworks ROME CAN; Cremona is the Lombard city famous for violin-makers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremona is a city in Lombardy, northern Italy, home of Stradivari.

clue.text: Winslow, for example, making comeback in celebrated action

indicators.note: making a comeback means the letters return, read backwards
in signals letters sitting inside the words celebrated action

explanation.surface: A man named Winslow returns in a famous deed.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden run TEDAC is in 'celebraTED ACtion', read backwards. Winslow is Terence Rattigan's 'The Winslow Boy', a naval trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronnie Winslow, Rattigan's Winslow Boy, is a naval college trainee expelled for theft.

clue.text: Odd gospel of Huns could be problem for Christian

indicators.note: could be says the preceding letters might form something else if rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange scripture from barbarian tribes troubles a believer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'could be' rearranges ODD GOSPEL OF HUNS. Christian is the hero of Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress, who sinks in this bog.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Pilgrim's Progress, the hero Christian falls into this bog of despair early in his journey.

clue.text: Artist stops just short of entrance

indicators.note: stopping just short means the final letter is lost

parts.note: ingress means an entrance or way in

explanation.surface: A painter halts just before the doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops just short of' drops the last S of INGRESS. Ingres was a French Neoclassical painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a nineteenth-century French painter.

clue.text: Source of special egg in large quantity

indicators.note: in puts the urging word inside the large quantity

parts.note: tons, or a ton, is informal for a large quantity
to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: Where an exceptional egg comes from, in bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition shares 'special' with the wordplay: the fish's roe is caviar, the special egg.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is the fish whose roe is caviar, the prized luxury eggs.
